references.name: Karl Popper
references.desc: Falsificationism — science advances by disproving, not proving; The Logic of Scientific Discovery; Taleb's intellectual hero

references.name: George Soros
references.desc: Popperian trader; obsessively self-critical; gateway to Popper's philosophy for Taleb

references.name: Daniel Kahneman & Amos Tversky
references.desc: Most influential economists by journal citations; proved humans systematically fail at rational thinking under uncertainty

references.name: David Hume
references.desc: The problem of induction — empirical observations can mislead without proper method; the black swan of inference

references.name: Francis Bacon
references.desc: Shifted science from scholasticism to empirical observation; warned against confirmation bias

references.name: Victor Niederhoffer
references.desc: The Education of a Speculator; finance's empiricist who challenged the efficient market hypothesis, then spectacularly blew up

references.name: Robert Shiller
references.desc: Showed markets are far more volatile than efficient market theory predicts; Irrational Exuberance

references.name: Harry Markowitz
references.desc: Nobel laureate for Modern Portfolio Theory; Taleb questions the real-world applicability of the models

references.name: Robert Merton & Myron Scholes
references.desc: Nobel laureates whose Long-Term Capital Management fund collapsed — proving models break under extreme randomness

references.name: Louis Bachelier
references.desc: First mathematical model of market randomness (1900); underestimated by Poincaré

references.name: Auguste Comte
references.desc: Founder of positivism; believed science could predict everything — exactly the overconfidence Taleb critiques

references.name: Friedrich Hayek
references.desc: Taleb's friend; endorsed capitalism as a system where prices disseminate information that socialism would choke

references.name: Marcel Proust
references.desc: In Search of Lost Time; Taleb's literary touchstone for memory, randomness, and the passage of time

references.name: Jean Buridan
references.desc: 14th-century philosopher; Buridan's Donkey paradox on decision-making under equal options

references.name: Solon
references.desc: Ancient Greek lawgiver who warned Croesus: judge no man happy until he is dead — the original lesson on survivorship bias
